# evidence-emitter

> Composes the installed loomground assurance components into one DSSE-signed in-toto Statement and ships an offline verifier, so anyone can re-check, from the package's bytes alone, what governance an agent applied to an action.

## Problem
A governance decision (a compliance-fleet directive, a privacy-shield egress verdict) is only as trustworthy as the evidence someone can re-check afterward, offline, without trusting the emitting agent again. evidence-emitter digest-binds the decision, embeds whichever assurance components are installed (each probed independently, absent ones marked as such rather than faked), and signs the result — a package a verifier can check from bytes alone.

## Install
```
pip install "evidence-emitter @ git+https://github.com/flxk1/evidence-emitter@v0.1.0"
```
Import name `evidence_emitter`. Base install has zero hard dependencies. Optional extras:
- `.[canonical]` — `rfc8785` (RFC 8785 JSON canonicalization; a stdlib approximation is used when absent)
- `.[ed25519]` — `cryptography` (production Ed25519 signing/verification; key material supplied by the host)
- `.[assurance]` — the loomground assurance components this package composes, when present
- `.[dev]` — `pytest` plus the above

## Usage
```python
from evidence_emitter import emit, verify, EvidenceContext, DevSigner

package = emit(
    subject,                     # an a2a-compliance decision or a privacy-shield ScanReport
    components=None,             # optional allowlist of component keys; others are marked absent
    signer=DevSigner(),          # default; a production signer supplies its own key
    context=EvidenceContext(...) # the governance inputs each present component attests
)

report = verify(package)         # offline re-check
report.ok                        # bool
report.summary()                 # one-line human summary
```
`emit(subject, *, kind=None, components=None, signer=None, context=None, issued_at=None) -> EvidencePackage`. `verify(package, *, signer=None) -> VerdictReport`. `EvidencePackage.to_dict()` / `.from_dict()` round-trip the DSSE envelope.

CLI:
```
evidence-emit   <subject.json> [--kind KIND] [--context context.json] [--components a,b] [-o out.json]
evidence-verify <package.json>
```
Both default to the non-production dev signer; a production signing key is supplied to the library API, never on a command line.

## Contracts
| Surface | Definition |
|---|---|
| Recognised subjects | an a2a-compliance control `Message`/`SteerRuling`, or a privacy-shield `ScanReport` — matched structurally, without importing either package |
| Assurance components | `evidence_emitter.components` — `governance-certification`, `oversight-certificate`, `enforcement-posture`, `effect-reconciliation`, `norm-freshness`, `obligation-discharge`, `5d-nd`; each contributes one attestation/computation/grounding section, or is marked absent |
| Signing seam | `evidence_emitter.signer` — `DevSigner` (HMAC dev stand-in, `production=False`), `Ed25519Signer`/`Ed25519Verifier` (host-supplied key via `from_private_pem`/`from_public_pem`); any `Signer` needs `key_id`, `algorithm`, `production`, `sign`, `verify`, `descriptor` |
| Canonical bytes | `evidence_emitter.canonical` — RFC 8785 (JCS) when available, else a named stdlib sort-keys approximation; a verifier missing the named scheme fails closed |
| Subject normalization | `evidence_emitter.subjects` |
| Skill entry | `skills/evidence-emitter/SKILL.md` |

Every present section is re-checked through its own component's verifier where installed, and a generic DSSE check otherwise; a package signed by the dev signer verifies but is reported non-production.
